source.text: Γνωρίζομεν δὲ ὑμῖν, ἀδελφοί, τὴν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ τὴν δεδομένην ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῆς Μακεδονίας, ὅτι ἐν πολλῇ δοκιμῇ θλίψεως ἡ περισσεία τῆς χαρᾶς αὐτῶν καὶ ἡ κατὰ βάθους πτωχεία αὐτῶν ἐπερίσσευσεν εἰς τὸ πλοῦτος τῆς ἁπλότητος αὐτῶν·

records.literal_gloss: We make known and to you, brothers, the grace of the God the [grace] having been given in the churches of the Macedonia, \v 2 that in much testing of affliction the abundance of the joy of them and the according to depth poverty of them abounded into the riches of the generosity of them;

en.L: Now we make known to you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, the grace of God that has been given in the churches of Macedonia, \v 2 that in a great test of affliction the abundance of their joy and their poverty down to the depths overflowed into the riches of their generosity.
en.B: We want you to know, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, about the grace God has given to the churches of Macedonia. \v 2 Hardship has put them to a severe test, yet their joy has overflowed, and their deep poverty has spilled over into riches of generosity.
en.R: We want to tell you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, about the grace God has given to the churches in Macedonia. \v 2 They have had a lot of trouble, and it has tested them hard. They are very poor. But they are so full of joy that they have given with open hands, as freely as if they were rich.

fr.L: Nous vous faisons connaître, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, la grâce de Dieu qui a été donnée dans les églises de Macédoine : \v 2 dans une grande épreuve de détresse, l’abondance de leur joie et leur profonde pauvreté ont débordé en richesse de leur générosité.
fr.B: Nous voulons que vous sachiez, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, quelle grâce Dieu a accordée aux églises de Macédoine. \v 2 Les épreuves qu’elles ont traversées ont été pour elles un test sévère, et pourtant leur joie a débordé, et leur extrême pauvreté s’est répandue en une riche générosité.
fr.R: Nous voulons vous parler, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, de la grâce que Dieu a donnée aux églises de Macédoine. \v 2 Ces croyants ont eu beaucoup de difficultés, qui les ont durement mis à l’épreuve. Ils sont très pauvres. Mais ils sont si pleins de joie qu’ils ont donné à pleines mains, aussi librement que s’ils étaient riches.

es.L: Ahora bien, {{plural_you:les|os}} hacemos saber, hermanos, la gracia de Dios que ha sido dada en las iglesias de Macedonia, \v 2 que en una gran prueba de aflicción, la abundancia de su gozo y su profunda pobreza abundaron en la riqueza de su generosidad.
es.B: Hermanos, queremos que {{plural_you:conozcan|conozcáis}} la gracia que Dios ha dado a las iglesias de Macedonia. \v 2 Las dificultades los han sometido a una dura prueba, pero su alegría se ha desbordado, y su extrema pobreza ha rebosado en una gran riqueza de generosidad.
es.R: Hermanos, queremos {{plural_you:contarles|contaros}} acerca de la gracia que Dios ha dado a las iglesias de Macedonia. \v 2 Han tenido muchos problemas, y eso los ha puesto a prueba con dureza. Son muy pobres. Pero están tan llenos de alegría que han dado con las manos abiertas, con tanta generosidad como si fueran ricos.

decisions.choice: the churches of the Roman province of Macedonia, north of Achaia
decisions.reason: Macedonia was the Roman province north of Greece, where Paul founded the churches of Philippi, Thessalonica and Berea (Acts 16-17). Paul had come there from Asia and met Titus there (2:13; 7:5-6), and he is writing from there. These churches were taking part in Paul's collection for the poor believers in Jerusalem (Romans 15:26; 1 Corinthians 16:1-4), which is the subject of chapters 8 and 9.

decisions.choice: the grace of God shown in what it did: it moved the Macedonians to give
alternatives: a gift of money that God gave to the Macedonians
decisions.reason: Paul begins with God's grace, not with the Macedonians' generosity. Their giving is the visible result of God's grace at work in them. The word χάριν comes back again and again in these chapters (verses 4, 6, 7, 9, 16, 19; 9:8, 14, 15), and Paul plays on it: God's grace, the gift that grace produces, and thanks to God for it.

decisions.choice: generosity: wholehearted, open-handed giving
decisions.reason: ἁπλότητος first means singleness or sincerity, a heart that is not divided. Used of giving it means giving without holding back or calculating (Romans 12:8; 2 Corinthians 9:11, 13). Here the context of rich giving out of poverty makes generosity the sense.

decisions.choice: a severe test that came by way of affliction
alternatives: a great proof given by their affliction
decisions.reason: δοκιμῇ is a test, or the proof that comes from passing one; the genitive θλίψεως says what tested them: hardship, probably persecution and poverty (1 Thessalonians 1:6; 2:14). Their joy and their giving came in the middle of it, not after it.

decisions.choice: poverty that went to the very bottom: extreme poverty
alternatives: poverty that is deep down, hidden
decisions.reason: κατὰ βάθους means "down to the depth". Paul sets the depth of their poverty against the riches of their generosity: two things that should cancel each other out (joy in affliction, riches out of poverty) together produce something rich. Verse 9 uses the same poor-rich contrast for Christ.

decisions.choice: fellow believers, women and men
decisions.reason: ἀδελφοί is masculine plural, the ordinary way to address a mixed group of men and women together.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: Paul writes to the whole church, women and men. "Brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: affliction (L); hardship (B); trouble (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for this word in 1 and 2 Corinthians. "Suffering" is kept for a different word.

decisions.choice: they have given with open hands, as freely as if they were rich
alternatives: their poverty overflowed into the riches of their generosity
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the Macedonians gave money, which is what "generosity" means here (verse 3), and keeps the poor-rich contrast as a comparison.

decisions.choice: {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} for the readers; les églises de Macédoine, lowercase (for chapters 8-11)
decisions.reason: As in English, Paul writes to the whole church, women and men, with "frères" available as the traditional form. "Église" takes a small letter for local congregations and a capital only for the whole body of believers (style guide section 9).

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As in 1:8, Spanish "hermanos" already includes the sisters, so the English gender setting has no Spanish counterpart.

source.text: ὅτι κατὰ δύναμιν, μαρτυρῶ, καὶ παρὰ δύναμιν, αὐθαίρετοι μετὰ πολλῆς παρακλήσεως δεόμενοι ἡμῶν, τὴν χάριν καὶ τὴν κοινωνίαν τῆς διακονίας τῆς εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους καὶ οὐ καθὼς ἠλπίσαμεν ἀλλ’ ἑαυτοὺς ἔδωκαν πρῶτον τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ ἡμῖν διὰ θελήματος θεοῦ, εἰς τὸ παρακαλέσαι ἡμᾶς Τίτον ἵνα καθὼς προενήρξατο οὕτως καὶ ἐπιτελέσῃ εἰς ὑμᾶς καὶ τὴν χάριν ταύτην·

records.literal_gloss: That according to ability, I testify, and beyond ability, of their own accord, \v 4 with much appeal begging us the grace and the sharing of the ministry the [one] for the holy ones, \v 5 and not as we hoped but themselves they gave first to the Lord and to us through [the] will of God, \v 6 for the to urge us Titus that just as he began beforehand so also he should complete toward you also the grace this;

en.L: For according to [their] ability, I testify, and beyond [their] ability, [they gave] of their own accord, \v 4 begging us with much appeal for the grace and the partnership of the ministry for the holy ones; \v 5 and not as we had hoped, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and to us through [the] will of God, \v 6 so that we urged Titus that, just as he had made a beginning before, so he should also complete among you this grace as well.
en.B: I can vouch for it: they gave all they could, and more than they could, and they did it of their own free will. \v 4 Again and again they appealed to us, begging for the favor of a share in the relief for God's holy people. \v 5 It went beyond anything we had hoped for. Before anything else they gave themselves to the Lord, and then, because God willed it, to us. \v 6 That is why we have asked Titus, who got this started among you in the first place, to see this gift of grace through to the end with you as well.
en.R: I can tell you that they gave as much as they could, and even more. No one made them do it. \v 4 They kept begging us for the special favor of having a part in helping God's people in Jerusalem. \v 5 They did more than we had hoped. First they gave themselves to the Lord. Then, because God wanted it, they gave themselves to us too. \v 6 Titus was the one who had started this work of collecting money among you. So we asked him to help you finish this generous gift.

fr.L: Car selon [leurs] moyens, j’en rends témoignage, et au-delà de [leurs] moyens, [ils ont donné] d’eux-mêmes, \v 4 nous demandant avec beaucoup d’insistance la grâce et la participation au ministère en faveur des saints ; \v 5 et non comme nous l’avions espéré, mais ils se sont donnés eux-mêmes d’abord au Seigneur et à nous, par la volonté de Dieu, \v 6 de sorte que nous avons exhorté Tite à achever aussi chez vous cette grâce-là, comme il l’avait commencée auparavant.
fr.B: Je peux en témoigner : ils ont donné tout ce qu’ils pouvaient, et plus encore, et ils l’ont fait de leur plein gré. \v 4 Ils nous ont demandé avec insistance, encore et encore, la faveur de prendre part au secours destiné au peuple saint de Dieu. \v 5 Ils sont allés au-delà de tout ce que nous espérions. Avant tout, ils se sont donnés eux-mêmes au Seigneur, puis à nous, parce que Dieu le voulait. \v 6 C’est pourquoi nous avons demandé à Tite, qui avait commencé cette œuvre chez vous, de mener aussi à son terme ce don de grâce.
fr.R: Je peux vous dire qu’ils ont donné autant qu’ils pouvaient, et même plus. Personne ne les a obligés à le faire. \v 4 Ils n’arrêtaient pas de nous supplier de leur accorder la faveur spéciale de participer à l’aide pour le peuple de Dieu à Jérusalem. \v 5 Ils ont fait plus que ce que nous espérions. D’abord, ils se sont donnés eux-mêmes au Seigneur. Ensuite, parce que Dieu le voulait, ils se sont donnés à nous aussi. \v 6 C’est Tite qui avait commencé chez vous ce travail de collecte d’argent. Alors nous lui avons demandé de vous aider à achever ce don généreux.

es.L: Porque doy testimonio de que, según [sus] posibilidades, y más allá de [sus] posibilidades, [dieron] por su propia iniciativa, \v 4 rogándonos con mucha insistencia la gracia y la participación en el ministerio para los santos; \v 5 y no como esperábamos, sino que se dieron a sí mismos primero al Señor y a nosotros por [la] voluntad de Dios, \v 6 de modo que exhortamos a Tito a que, así como había comenzado antes, también completara entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} esta gracia.
es.B: Puedo dar fe de ello: dieron todo lo que podían, y más de lo que podían, y lo hicieron por su propia voluntad. \v 4 Una y otra vez nos rogaron, suplicándonos el favor de tener parte en la ayuda para el pueblo santo de Dios. \v 5 Fue más allá de todo lo que esperábamos. Antes que nada se dieron a sí mismos al Señor, y luego, porque Dios así lo quiso, a nosotros. \v 6 Por eso le hemos pedido a Tito, que fue quien comenzó esto entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, que lleve también a su término este don de la gracia.
es.R: Puedo {{plural_you:decirles|deciros}} que dieron todo lo que podían, y aun más. Nadie los obligó a hacerlo. \v 4 Nos rogaban una y otra vez que les concediéramos el favor especial de tener parte en la ayuda para el pueblo de Dios en Jerusalén. \v 5 Hicieron más de lo que esperábamos. Primero se entregaron al Señor. Luego, porque Dios así lo quería, se entregaron también a nosotros. \v 6 Tito fue quien comenzó entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} este trabajo de recoger dinero. Así que le pedimos que {{plural_you:les|os}} ayude a terminar este generoso regalo.

decisions.choice: "they gave" is understood in verse 3 from the verb in verse 5
decisions.reason: Verses 3-4 have no main verb of their own; Paul piles up descriptions of the Macedonians and reaches the verb ἔδωκαν ("they gave") only in verse 5. The sense of verse 3 is plain: they gave as far as they were able, and beyond. αὐθαίρετοι means acting by one's own choice, without being asked or pressed.

decisions.choice: favor, privilege: a kindness they asked to be shown, the opportunity to give
decisions.reason: χάριν is the word for grace. Here it is something the Macedonians ask Paul for: the favor of being allowed to take part. It is linked by "and" to the sharing that follows, so the two together mean the privilege of sharing. Paul uses the same word in verse 1 for God's grace that moved them, so their request is grace answering grace.

decisions.choice: partnership: having a share in a common work
decisions.reason: κοινωνίαν is the partnership word of Philippians 1:5, where the Philippians shared in Paul's work by giving. Here the Macedonians want a share in the collection.

decisions.choice: the collection for the poor believers in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: διακονίας is service of any kind. Here it is the relief fund Paul was gathering from his Gentile churches for the poor among the believers in Jerusalem (Romans 15:25-27, 31; 1 Corinthians 16:1-4; Galatians 2:10; Acts 24:17). "The holy ones" are the believers in Jerusalem, as in Romans 15:25-26.

decisions.choice: first of all they gave themselves to the Lord, and then to Paul
alternatives: they were the first churches to give
decisions.reason: πρῶτον most likely means first in importance as well as in order: before they gave money, they gave themselves, to the Lord and then to Paul's work, as God willed. It does not mean that they were the first churches to give; verse 10 says Corinth began before them.

decisions.choice: this act of grace: the collection, as a generous gift that grace produces
alternatives: the grace of God in general
decisions.reason: τὴν χάριν ταύτην points to the collection itself. Paul calls it a χάριν because it is a generous gift, and because it is grace at work (verse 1). Verses 7 and 19 use the word in the same way.

decisions.choice: Titus had started the collection at Corinth on an earlier visit
alternatives: Titus began it on the visit described in 7:6-15
decisions.reason: Paul says only that Titus "made a beginning before". Since Corinth had started a year earlier (verse 10; 9:2), Titus probably organized the collection on a visit before the one in chapter 7. Now he is to finish it.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: the sentence goes straight on to verse 5
alternatives: some manuscripts add "that we should receive" after verse 4
decisions.reason: Some later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add a verb meaning "that we should receive" at the end of verse 4, to make the sentence easier. The older manuscripts do not have it. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: grace (L); favor (B); special favor (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "grace" so that the reader can trace Paul's play on the word through the chapter. Balanced and Readable say what is being asked for (m2): the favor of being allowed to take part.

decisions.choice: grace (L); gift of grace (B); generous gift (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word. Balanced says "gift of grace", which keeps the key term and its link with God's grace in verse 1 while making clear that a gift is meant (m6). Readable says "generous gift".

decisions.choice: ministry (L); relief (B); helping (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering is "ministry", which Literal keeps. Here it means a relief fund (m4), and "ministry" would make most readers think of preaching, so Balanced says "relief" and Readable "helping".

decisions.choice: holy ones (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering of this word, as in 1:1.

decisions.choice: in Jerusalem; this work of collecting money
alternatives: the holy ones; he had begun
decisions.reason: Readable says who the holy ones were and what Titus had begun (m4, m7).

decisions.choice: la grâce (L); la faveur (B), la faveur spéciale (R) in 8:4; le don de grâce (B), le don généreux (R) for the collection (for chapters 8-9)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "grâce" so that Paul's play on the word can be traced through the two chapters. Balanced and Readable say what is meant each time, as the English does: the favor of being allowed to give, and the gift that grace produces.

decisions.choice: le ministère (L); le secours (B); l’aide, aider (R) for the collection; les saints (L), le peuple saint de Dieu (B), le peuple de Dieu (R) (for chapters 8-9)
decisions.reason: "Ministère" is the letter's word for this noun and Literal keeps it; for a relief fund it would suggest preaching, so Balanced says "le secours" (the English "relief") and Readable "l’aide". The holy ones follow the style guide's term sheet.

decisions.choice: gracia (L); el favor, este don de la gracia (B); el favor especial, este generoso regalo (R)
decisions.reason: In chapters 8-9 the grace word names the privilege of giving and the gift itself (meaning decisions). Literal keeps "gracia" so the word can be traced; Balanced and Readable say what is meant, as the English does.

decisions.choice: ministerio (L); la ayuda (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the service word names the collection for the believers in Jerusalem; "ministerio" alone would suggest preaching, so Balanced and Readable say "ayuda", as the English says relief and helping.

source.text: ἀλλ’ ὥσπερ ἐν παντὶ περισσεύετε, πίστει καὶ λόγῳ καὶ γνώσει καὶ πάσῃ σπουδῇ καὶ τῇ ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐν ὑμῖν ἀγάπῃ, ἵνα καὶ ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ χάριτι περισσεύητε.

records.literal_gloss: But just as in everything you abound, in faith and speech and knowledge and all earnestness and in the from us in you love, that also in this the grace you abound.

en.L: But just as you abound in everything, in faith and speech and knowledge and all eagerness, and in the love [that is] from us in you, [see] that you abound in this grace also.
en.B: You overflow in everything else: faith, speech, knowledge, eagerness of every kind, and the love from us that now lives in you. Now see that you overflow in this gift of grace as well.
en.R: You have more than enough of everything: faith, speaking, knowledge, eagerness of every kind, and the love we brought you. So make sure that you overflow in this generous giving too.

fr.L: Mais de même que vous abondez en tout, en foi, en parole, en connaissance, en tout empressement et dans l’amour [qui vient] de nous [et qui est] en vous, [veillez] à abonder aussi dans cette grâce.
fr.B: Vous avez tout en abondance : la foi, la parole, la connaissance, un empressement de toute sorte, et l’amour qui vient de nous et qui vit maintenant en vous. Veillez donc à donner aussi en abondance dans ce don de grâce.
fr.R: Vous avez plus qu’assez de tout : la foi, la parole, la connaissance, l’empressement en toutes choses, et l’amour que nous vous avons apporté. Alors faites en sorte de donner aussi avec abondance.

es.L: Pero así como en todo {{plural_you:abundan|abundáis}}, en fe, en palabra, en conocimiento, en toda diligencia y en el amor [que va] de nosotros a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, [{{plural_you:procuren|procurad}}] abundar también en esta gracia.
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} {{plural_you:rebosan|rebosáis}} en todo lo demás: en fe, en palabra, en conocimiento, en toda clase de diligencia y en el amor que de nosotros ha llegado a vivir en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Procuren|Procurad}}, pues, rebosar también en este don de la gracia.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes tienen|Vosotros tenéis}} de sobra de todo: fe, palabra, conocimiento, diligencia de toda clase, y el amor que nosotros {{plural_you:les|os}} llevamos. Así que {{plural_you:procuren|procurad}} rebosar también en esta manera generosa de dar.

decisions.choice: a gentle command: see that you excel in this too
alternatives: a purpose clause depending on verse 6
decisions.reason: ἵνα with the subjunctive can express a request or command, as in Ephesians 5:33. Paul turns from the Macedonians to the Corinthians: they already abound in many things, so let them abound in this.

decisions.choice: gifts the Corinthians were proud of
decisions.reason: Paul thanked God that the Corinthians were rich "in all speech and all knowledge" (1 Corinthians 1:5), gifts they prized highly (1 Corinthians 8:1; 12-14). He now asks them to add generosity to the list.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the love from us in you", Paul's love that lives in them
alternatives: "your love for us", found in many manuscripts
decisions.reason: The manuscripts are divided between "from us in you" and "from you in us", which differ by one letter in each pronoun. Many manuscripts have "your love for us", which is the easier reading after 7:7, 12. SBLGNT follows the harder reading: the love Paul showed them, which has taken root in them. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: this act of grace: the collection
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, ταύτῃ τῇ χάριτι is the collection, a gift that is itself the work of grace. The repetition keeps the link with God's grace in verse 1 and Christ's grace in verse 9.

decisions.choice: eagerness, earnest effort
decisions.reason: σπουδῇ is zeal that puts effort into something. It comes back in verses 8, 16 and 22, and in 7:11-12.

decisions.choice: grace (L); gift of grace (B); generous giving (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word; Balanced says "gift of grace" as in verse 6, and Readable says what the grace consists of here (m4).

decisions.choice: overflow (B); more than enough, overflow (R)
decisions.reason: The same verb opens and closes the sentence. Balanced and Readable use words of abundance, which match verse 2, rather than "excel", which suggests competition.

decisions.choice: the love we brought you
alternatives: the love from us in you
decisions.reason: Readable gives the SBLGNT reading (m3) in plain words.

source.text: Οὐ κατ’ ἐπιταγὴν λέγω ἀλλὰ διὰ τῆς ἑτέρων σπουδῆς καὶ τὸ τῆς ὑμετέρας ἀγάπης γνήσιον δοκιμάζων·

records.literal_gloss: Not according to command I speak but through the of others earnestness also the of your love genuineness testing;

en.L: I do not speak by way of command, but [I am] testing through the eagerness of others the genuineness of your love also.
en.B: I am not giving you an order. I am using the eagerness of others to put your love to the test and show that it is real.
en.R: I am not ordering you to give. But other believers have been so eager to help, and I want to see whether your love is just as real.

fr.L: Je ne parle pas par mode de commandement, mais [je mets] à l’épreuve, par l’empressement des autres, l’authenticité de votre amour aussi.
fr.B: Je ne vous donne pas un ordre. Je me sers de l’empressement des autres pour mettre votre amour à l’épreuve et montrer qu’il est vrai.
fr.R: Je ne vous ordonne pas de donner. Mais d’autres croyants ont été très empressés d’aider, et je veux voir si votre amour est aussi vrai.

es.L: No hablo como quien da una orden, sino que, por medio de la diligencia de otros, [estoy] poniendo a prueba también la sinceridad de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} amor.
es.B: No {{plural_you:les|os}} estoy dando una orden. Estoy usando la diligencia de otros para poner a prueba {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} amor y mostrar que es auténtico.
es.R: No {{plural_you:les|os}} estoy ordenando que {{plural_you:den|deis}}. Pero otros creyentes han estado muy dispuestos a ayudar, y quiero ver si el amor de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} es igual de auténtico.

decisions.choice: an appeal, not an order
alternatives: Paul has no authority to command them
decisions.reason: Paul could give orders (1 Corinthians 7:10; Philemon 8), but for a gift he chooses not to. A gift that is ordered is no longer freely given (9:7). He uses the same words in 1 Corinthians 7:6.

decisions.choice: testing so as to prove genuine
decisions.reason: δοκιμάζων is to test something, as metal is tested, in order to show that it is genuine. It belongs to the same family as the "test" of verse 2: the Macedonians were tested by hardship; the Corinthians are tested by the Macedonians' example.

decisions.choice: the eagerness of others: the Macedonians
decisions.reason: The "others" are the churches of verses 1-5.

decisions.choice: to give; to help
alternatives: I am not speaking by command
decisions.reason: Readable says what the command would have been about and what the others were eager for.

source.text: γινώσκετε γὰρ τὴν χάριν τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὅτι δι’ ὑμᾶς ἐπτώχευσεν πλούσιος ὤν, ἵνα ὑμεῖς τῇ ἐκείνου πτωχείᾳ πλουτήσητε.

records.literal_gloss: You know for the grace of the Lord of us Jesus Christ, that for the sake of you he became poor rich being, so that you by the of that one poverty might become rich.

en.L: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, that for your sake {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} became poor, being rich, so that you, by the poverty of that one, might become rich.
en.B: After all, you know the grace of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}: rich as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} became poor for your sake, so that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} poverty might make you rich.
en.R: You know the grace of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. He was rich, but for your sake {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} became poor. And because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} became poor, you can become rich.

fr.L: Car vous connaissez la grâce de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} : pour vous {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est devenu pauvre, étant riche, afin que vous, par la pauvreté de celui-là, vous deveniez riches.
fr.B: Vous connaissez en effet la grâce de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} : {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui était riche, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est devenu pauvre à cause de vous, pour que {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} pauvreté vous rende riches.
fr.R: Vous connaissez la grâce de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. Il était riche, mais à cause de vous, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est devenu pauvre. Et parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est devenu pauvre, vous pouvez devenir riches.

es.L: Porque {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} la gracia de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} que por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} se hizo pobre, siendo rico, para que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, por la pobreza de aquel, {{plural_you:llegaran|llegarais}} a ser ricos.
es.B: Al fin y al cabo, {{plural_you:ustedes conocen|vosotros conocéis}} la gracia de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}: siendo rico, se hizo pobre por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, para que {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pobreza {{plural_you:los|os}} hiciera ricos.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes conocen|Vosotros conocéis}} la gracia de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. Él era rico, pero por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} se hizo pobre. Y porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se hizo pobre, {{plural_you:ustedes pueden|vosotros podéis}} llegar a ser ricos.

decisions.choice: Christ, who was rich, became poor: he left the riches that were his and took on a human life of poverty and death
alternatives: Jesus was rich during his earthly life and gave his wealth away
Jesus became poor only by being born into a poor family
decisions.reason: Paul does not mean Jesus' earthly money; nothing in the Gospels suggests he was ever wealthy. The riches are what belonged to him before he became human, and the poverty is his becoming human and dying on the cross. Philippians 2:6-8 says the same: being in the form of God, he emptied himself and took the form of a slave. The present participle ὤν ("being") states what he was when he chose to become poor.

decisions.choice: grace: Christ's free, generous self-giving
decisions.reason: Here χάριν is Christ's undeserved kindness in giving himself. Paul sets it before the Corinthians as the pattern for their own giving: the grace of verse 1, which moved the Macedonians to give, has its source here.

decisions.choice: become rich: share in all that Christ gives, not in money
decisions.reason: The riches are the blessings of salvation: being made right with God, the Spirit, and every gift (1 Corinthians 1:5; 2 Corinthians 6:10). Paul is not promising wealth; the Macedonians gave out of deep poverty (verse 2).

decisions.choice: for your sake: on your behalf and for your good
decisions.reason: δι ὑμᾶς puts the readers at the center. Christ's poverty was chosen for them; that is why it carries weight in an appeal for them to give.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}
decisions.reason: Pronouns for Christ follow the deity_pronoun setting. Literal keeps "that one" for the Greek demonstrative.

decisions.choice: rich as he was, he became poor for your sake, so that his poverty might make you rich
alternatives: though he was rich, for your sake he became poor
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "rich" first, as English naturally states the earlier state first, and ends on the purpose: the readers' riches.

decisions.choice: Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} (L), Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} (B, R); every pronoun for Christ under deity_pronoun, subject "il" included ("{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui était riche") (for chapters 8-11)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians: French must write the subject pronoun, so "il" for Christ carries the span wherever the English "he" does, and "lui" takes one where French needs it. Literal keeps "celui-là" for the Greek demonstrative without a span, as the English keeps "that one". A pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital.

decisions.choice: aquel, with no span
decisions.reason: "Aquel" is a demonstrative, as the Greek "that one" is, not a personal pronoun; it carries no deity_pronoun span, as the English "that one" carries none.

source.text: καὶ γνώμην ἐν τούτῳ δίδωμι· τοῦτο γὰρ ὑμῖν συμφέρει, οἵτινες οὐ μόνον τὸ ποιῆσαι ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ θέλειν προενήρξασθε ἀπὸ πέρυσι·

records.literal_gloss: And an opinion in this I give; this for to you is beneficial, who not only the to do but also the to want began beforehand from last year;

en.L: And I give [my] opinion in this [matter]: for this is beneficial for you, who began beforehand, from last year, not only to do but also to want [it].
en.B: I offer my advice on this, because it is in your interest. You made a start last year, ahead of others, and it was not only a matter of doing something: you wanted to do it.
en.R: This is what I think you should do, and it will be good for you. You started giving last year, before anyone else did, and you really wanted to do it.

fr.L: Et c’est un avis que je donne en cela ; car cela vous est profitable, à vous qui avez commencé les premiers, dès l’an dernier, non seulement à faire, mais aussi à vouloir.
fr.B: Je vous donne mon avis sur ce point, car c’est dans votre intérêt. Vous avez commencé l’an dernier, avant les autres, et il ne s’agissait pas seulement de faire quelque chose : vous vouliez le faire.
fr.R: Voici ce que je pense que vous devriez faire, et ce sera bon pour vous. Vous avez commencé à donner l’an dernier, avant tout le monde, et vous vouliez vraiment le faire.

es.L: Y en esto doy [mi] opinión; porque esto {{plural_you:les|os}} conviene a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, que {{plural_you:comenzaron|comenzasteis}} antes, desde el año pasado, no solo a hacer[lo], sino también a quererlo.
es.B: En esto {{plural_you:les|os}} doy mi consejo, porque es para {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} bien. {{plural_you:Ustedes comenzaron|Vosotros comenzasteis}} el año pasado, antes que otros, y no se trataba solo de hacer algo: {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:querían|queríais}} hacerlo.
es.R: Esto es lo que pienso que {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} hacer, y será bueno para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Comenzaron|Comenzasteis}} a dar el año pasado, antes que nadie, y de verdad {{plural_you:querían|queríais}} hacerlo.

decisions.choice: advice, an opinion offered
decisions.reason: γνώμην is a considered opinion, as in 1 Corinthians 7:25, 40. It continues verse 8: Paul advises rather than commands.

decisions.choice: they began before others, and they wanted to give, not only acted
alternatives: they began wanting before they began doing
decisions.reason: The order "not only to do but also to want" is surprising, since wanting comes before doing. Paul probably means that the Corinthians were the first to act, and more than that, the first to be eager about it (9:2). The prefix of προενήρξασθε ("began beforehand") means they began before the Macedonians.

decisions.choice: since last year: about a year before this letter
decisions.reason: πέρυσι means last year. Depending on the calendar Paul uses, this could be anything from a few months to more than a year earlier. Paul speaks of the same start in 9:2, and 1 Corinthians 16:1-4 gives his first instructions about it.

decisions.choice: to start giving
decisions.reason: Readable names what they began to do.

source.text: νυνὶ δὲ καὶ τὸ ποιῆσαι ἐπιτελέσατε, ὅπως καθάπερ ἡ προθυμία τοῦ θέλειν οὕτως καὶ τὸ ἐπιτελέσαι ἐκ τοῦ ἔχειν.

records.literal_gloss: Now and also the doing complete, so that just as the readiness of the to want so also the to complete out of the to have.

en.L: But now also complete the doing [of it], so that just as [there was] the readiness to want [it], so also [there may be] the completing [of it] out of what [you] have.
en.B: Now bring the doing of it to an end as well. You were eager to want it; let the finishing show the same eagerness, giving out of whatever you have.
en.R: So now finish the job. You were eager to give, so now give what you can from what you have.

fr.L: Mais maintenant, achevez aussi de faire, afin que, de même qu’[il y a eu] l’empressement à vouloir, ainsi [il y ait] aussi l’achèvement, selon ce que [vous] avez.
fr.B: Maintenant, achevez aussi de le faire. Vous avez mis de l’empressement à le vouloir ; que l’achèvement montre le même empressement, en donnant selon ce que vous avez.
fr.R: Alors maintenant, terminez le travail. Vous aviez très envie de donner ; maintenant, donnez ce que vous pouvez, selon ce que vous avez.

es.L: Ahora, pues, {{plural_you:completen|completad}} también el hacer[lo], para que, así como [hubo] la disposición para quererlo, así también [haya] el completar[lo] según lo que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}.
es.B: Ahora {{plural_you:lleven|llevad}} también a término lo que {{plural_you:comenzaron|comenzasteis}}. Así como {{plural_you:estuvieron|estuvisteis}} dispuestos a quererlo, que el terminarlo muestre la misma disposición, dando de lo que {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}}.
es.R: Así que ahora {{plural_you:terminen|terminad}} el trabajo. {{plural_you:Estaban|Estabais}} deseosos de dar, así que ahora {{plural_you:den|dad}} lo que {{plural_you:puedan|podáis}} de lo que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}.

decisions.choice: readiness, eager willingness
decisions.reason: προθυμία is a readiness that is keen to act. Paul uses it again in verses 12 and 19 and in 9:2.

decisions.choice: out of what you have: in proportion to your means
decisions.reason: ἐκ τοῦ ἔχειν means giving according to what one has. Verse 12 explains it: God looks for what a person can give, not for what they lack.

decisions.choice: bring the doing of it to an end; the finishing
decisions.reason: The Greek repeats one verb, "complete". Balanced keeps the repetition with two forms of "finish" and "end" while making the sentence read naturally.

source.text: εἰ γὰρ ἡ προθυμία πρόκειται, καθὸ ἐὰν ἔχῃ εὐπρόσδεκτος, οὐ καθὸ οὐκ ἔχει.

records.literal_gloss: If for the readiness is present, according to whatever one may have [it is] acceptable, not according to what one does not have.

en.L: For if the readiness is present, [it is] acceptable according to whatever one has, not according to what one does not have.
en.B: When eagerness is there, a gift is welcomed for what the giver has, not judged by what the giver lacks.
en.R: If you really want to give, God is pleased with whatever you can give. He does not ask for what you do not have.

fr.L: Car si l’empressement est là, [il est] bien accueilli selon ce qu’on a, non selon ce qu’on n’a pas.
fr.B: Quand l’empressement est là, un don est bien accueilli selon ce que possède celui qui donne, et il n’est pas jugé d’après ce qu’il n’a pas.
fr.R: Si vous voulez vraiment donner, Dieu est content de tout ce que vous pouvez donner. Il ne vous demande pas ce que vous n’avez pas.

es.L: Porque si la disposición está presente, [es] aceptable según lo que uno tenga, no según lo que no tiene.
es.B: Cuando hay buena disposición, la ofrenda se acepta por lo que el que da tiene, no se juzga por lo que le falta.
es.R: Si de verdad {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} dar, a Dios le agrada lo que {{plural_you:puedan|podáis}} dar. Él no pide lo que no {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}.

decisions.choice: acceptable, welcomed: by God
alternatives: acceptable to Paul or to the churches
decisions.reason: εὐπρόσδεκτος is used of offerings that God accepts (Romans 15:16; compare 2 Corinthians 6:2). Paul does not name who accepts the gift, but the background is the giving of offerings to God.

decisions.choice: the measure of a gift is what the giver has
decisions.reason: The subject of ἔχῃ ("has") is left general: whoever is giving. The gift is judged by what that person has. The thought is like Jesus' words about the widow's offering (Mark 12:41-44).

decisions.choice: a gift is welcomed
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the subject unstated; Balanced supplies "a gift" and uses "the giver" for the general subject.

decisions.choice: God is pleased with
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who accepts the gift (m1).

source.text: οὐ γὰρ ἵνα ἄλλοις ἄνεσις, ὑμῖν θλῖψις· ἀλλ’ ἐξ ἰσότητος ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ τὸ ὑμῶν περίσσευμα εἰς τὸ ἐκείνων ὑστέρημα, ἵνα καὶ τὸ ἐκείνων περίσσευμα γένηται εἰς τὸ ὑμῶν ὑστέρημα, ὅπως γένηται ἰσότης·

records.literal_gloss: Not for that to others relief, to you affliction; but out of equality \v 14 in the now time the of you abundance for the of those need, so that also the of those abundance may become for the of you need, so that may become equality;

en.L: For [it is] not that [there should be] relief for others [and] affliction for you, but [it is a matter] of equality: \v 14 at the present time your abundance [is] for their need, so that their abundance also may come to be for your need, so that there may be equality.
en.B: The point is not to bring relief to others by bringing hardship on you. It is a matter of equality. \v 14 At this moment your surplus can meet their need, so that one day their surplus may meet yours. That way there is equality.
en.R: I do not want to make life easy for others and bring trouble on you. I want things to be fair. \v 14 Right now you have more than you need, so you can help them with what they lack. Then, at another time, when you are in need, they can help you with what they have. That way things will be fair for everyone.

fr.L: Car [il ne s’agit] pas que [ce soit] un soulagement pour d’autres [et] une détresse pour vous, mais [c’est une question] d’égalité : \v 14 dans le temps présent, votre abondance [sert] à leur manque, afin que leur abondance aussi serve à votre manque, afin qu’il y ait égalité.
fr.B: Il ne s’agit pas de soulager les autres en vous mettant dans la gêne. C’est une question d’égalité. \v 14 En ce moment, votre surplus peut combler leurs besoins, pour qu’un jour leur surplus comble les vôtres. Ainsi, il y a égalité.
fr.R: Je ne veux pas rendre la vie facile aux autres et vous causer des difficultés. Je veux que les choses soient justes. \v 14 En ce moment, vous avez plus que ce dont vous avez besoin, alors vous pouvez les aider pour ce qui leur manque. Puis, un autre jour, quand vous serez dans le besoin, ils pourront vous aider avec ce qu’ils ont. Ainsi, les choses seront justes pour tout le monde.

es.L: Porque no [es] que [haya] alivio para otros [y] aflicción para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, sino [que es cuestión] de igualdad: \v 14 en el tiempo presente, la abundancia de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} [es] para la necesidad de ellos, para que también la abundancia de ellos llegue a ser para la necesidad de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, de modo que haya igualdad.
es.B: No se trata de aliviar a otros {{plural_you:causándoles|causándoos}} dificultades a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Es una cuestión de igualdad. \v 14 En este momento, lo que a {{plural_you:ustedes les|vosotros os}} sobra puede cubrir lo que a ellos les falta, para que algún día lo que a ellos les sobre cubra lo que a {{plural_you:ustedes les|vosotros os}} falte. Así hay igualdad.
es.R: No quiero hacer la vida fácil a otros y {{plural_you:causarles|causaros}} problemas a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Quiero que las cosas sean justas. \v 14 Ahora mismo {{plural_you:ustedes tienen|vosotros tenéis}} más de lo que {{plural_you:necesitan|necesitáis}}, así que {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} ayudarlos con lo que les falta. Después, en otro momento, cuando {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} necesitados, ellos podrán {{plural_you:ayudarlos|ayudaros}} con lo que tengan. Así las cosas serán justas para todos.

decisions.choice: equality: a fair balance, in which no one has too much while others lack
decisions.reason: ἰσότης is equality or fairness. Paul does not ask the Corinthians to make themselves poor (verse 12), and he does not mean that everyone must own the same. He means that what one group has to spare should meet what another lacks, as the quotation in verse 15 shows.

decisions.choice: a future time when Jerusalem may help Corinth
alternatives: the spiritual blessings Corinth has already received from Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Paul says their abundance "may come to be" for your need. This most likely means that the roles could be reversed one day. In Romans 15:27 Paul says the Gentiles owe material help because they have shared in the Jews' spiritual blessings; some read that idea here, but here the help runs the other way and is still future.

decisions.choice: relief and hardship: financial ease and strain
decisions.reason: ἄνεσις is relief or ease, θλῖψις pressure or hardship; here they describe the burden of giving, not persecution.

decisions.choice: affliction (L); hardship (B); trouble (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for this word; the sense here is financial strain (m3).

decisions.choice: fair
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plainer word for the balance Paul describes (m1).

decisions.choice: one day
alternatives: their abundance may also be for your need
decisions.reason: Balanced makes clear that the reverse help lies in the future (m2).

decisions.choice: vous mettre dans la gêne (B)
decisions.reason: The hardship here is financial strain (m3). French "la gêne" says exactly that, where the Balanced word for this noun elsewhere, "les épreuves", would sound like a trial of faith.

source.text: καθὼς γέγραπται· Ὁ τὸ πολὺ οὐκ ἐπλεόνασεν, καὶ ὁ τὸ ὀλίγον οὐκ ἠλαττόνησεν.

records.literal_gloss: Just as it has been written, The [one] the much not had more, and the [one] the little not had less.

en.L: Just as it is written, "The [one who gathered] much did not have too much, and the [one who gathered] little did not have too little."
en.B: As it is written, "The one who gathered a lot had nothing extra, and the one who gathered a little did not go short."
en.R: It is like what the Scriptures say about the manna, the food God gave {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people in the desert: "Those who gathered a lot had no more than they needed, and those who gathered a little had all they needed."

fr.L: Selon qu’il est écrit : « Celui [qui avait ramassé] beaucoup n’a pas eu trop, et celui [qui avait ramassé] peu n’a pas eu trop peu. »
fr.B: Comme il est écrit : « Celui qui en avait ramassé beaucoup n’en avait pas en surplus, et celui qui en avait ramassé peu n’était pas à court. »
fr.R: C’est comme ce que disent les Écritures au sujet de la manne, la nourriture que Dieu a donnée à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple dans le désert : « Ceux qui en avaient ramassé beaucoup n’en avaient pas plus qu’il ne leur fallait, et ceux qui en avaient ramassé peu en avaient assez. »

es.L: Como está escrito: «El que [recogió] mucho no tuvo de más, y el que [recogió] poco no tuvo de menos».
es.B: Como está escrito: «Al que recogió mucho no le sobró nada, y al que recogió poco no le faltó nada».
es.R: Es como lo que dicen las Escrituras sobre el maná, el alimento que Dios dio a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo en el desierto: «Los que recogieron mucho no tuvieron más de lo que necesitaban, y los que recogieron poco tuvieron todo lo que necesitaban».

decisions.choice: a quotation of Exodus 16:18, about the manna
decisions.reason: When God fed Israel with manna in the wilderness, each person gathered what he could, but when it was measured, no one had too much and no one too little (Exodus 16:16-18). Paul's words follow the Greek Old Testament closely. God's provision in the wilderness is the picture of the equality Paul has in mind: what is gathered is shared so that all have enough.

decisions.choice: "the one who gathered much": the verb is understood
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "the one the much ... the one the little", as the Greek of Exodus does; the verb "gathered" comes from the story.

decisions.choice: it is written: it stands written
decisions.reason: γέγραπται is a perfect: what Scripture says stands and still speaks, as in 1 Corinthians 1:19, 31.

decisions.choice: [who gathered] (L); gathered (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb is supplied from Exodus 16 (m2).

decisions.choice: what the Scriptures say about the manna, the food God gave his people in the desert
decisions.reason: Readers need the story to understand the quotation (m1).

source.text: Χάρις δὲ τῷ θεῷ τῷ διδόντι τὴν αὐτὴν σπουδὴν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ Τίτου, ὅτι τὴν μὲν παράκλησιν ἐδέξατο, σπουδαιότερος δὲ ὑπάρχων αὐθαίρετος ἐξῆλθεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: Thanks but to the God the [one] giving the same earnestness for you in the heart of Titus, \v 17 that the indeed appeal he accepted, more earnest but being, of his own accord he went out to you.

en.L: But thanks [be] to God, who puts the same eagerness for you in the heart of Titus, \v 17 for he accepted [our] appeal, but being very eager, he is going out to you of his own accord.
en.B: But thanks be to God, who fills the heart of Titus with the same eager concern for you that I feel. \v 17 Titus welcomed our request, but more than that, he is so keen that he is setting out to you by his own choice.
en.R: We give thanks to God, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given Titus the same eager love for you that I have. \v 17 We asked Titus to go to you, and he agreed. But he really wanted to go anyway, so he is coming to you because he chose to.

fr.L: Mais grâce [soit rendue] à Dieu, qui met le même empressement pour vous dans le cœur de Tite, \v 17 car il a accepté [notre] appel, mais, étant très empressé, il part vers vous de lui-même.
fr.B: Mais grâce soit rendue à Dieu, qui remplit le cœur de Tite du même empressement que moi à votre égard. \v 17 Tite a bien accueilli notre demande, mais plus encore, il est si empressé qu’il part vous rejoindre de son propre choix.
fr.R: Nous remercions Dieu, parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a donné à Tite le même amour ardent que moi pour vous. \v 17 Nous avons demandé à Tite d’aller chez vous, et il a accepté. Mais il voulait vraiment y aller de toute façon, alors il vient chez vous parce qu’il l’a choisi.

es.L: Pero gracias [sean] a Dios, que pone la misma diligencia por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en el corazón de Tito, \v 17 porque aceptó [nuestra] exhortación, pero, estando muy deseoso, va a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} por su propia iniciativa.
es.B: Pero gracias a Dios, que llena el corazón de Tito del mismo interés que yo siento por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. \v 17 Tito aceptó nuestra petición, pero aún más: tiene tanto interés que va a {{plural_you:visitarlos|visitaros}} por decisión propia.
es.R: Damos gracias a Dios, porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le ha dado a Tito el mismo amor y el mismo interés por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que yo tengo. \v 17 Le pedimos a Tito que fuera a {{plural_you:verlos|veros}}, y aceptó. Pero de todos modos él quería ir, así que va a {{plural_you:visitarlos|visitaros}} porque así lo decidió.

decisions.choice: thanks: gratitude given to God
decisions.reason: Χάρις with "to God" and no verb is the set phrase for giving thanks, as in 2:14 and 9:15. Paul turns the chapter's key word once more: the grace God gives produces thanks returned to him.

decisions.choice: the same eagerness for the Corinthians that Paul has
alternatives: the same eagerness the Macedonians showed
decisions.reason: "The same" most likely compares Titus's zeal with Paul's own care for the church, which the letter has shown throughout (7:12). God is the one who gives it; the present participle διδόντι suggests he keeps putting it there.

decisions.choice: he is going: Titus is setting out as Paul writes, probably carrying this letter
decisions.reason: ἐξῆλθεν is past in form, but letter writers often wrote from the point of view of the reader, for whom the sending had already happened. Titus and the brothers of verses 18-22 are sent with the letter (9:3-5).

decisions.choice: of his own accord
decisions.reason: αὐθαίρετος is the word used of the Macedonians in verse 3: Titus was asked, but he would have gone anyway.

decisions.choice: thanks
decisions.reason: The key term is rendered "thanks" here because the sense is gratitude (m1), as in 2:14.

decisions.choice: that I feel (B); that I have (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose eagerness Titus shares (m2).

decisions.choice: eager love
decisions.reason: Readable describes Titus's zeal for the church in warmer, plainer words.

decisions.choice: grâce [soit rendue] à Dieu (L); grâce soit rendue à Dieu (B); Nous remercions Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: French can say thanks with the key word itself, "rendre grâce", so Literal and Balanced keep "grâce" in the sense of gratitude (m1) and the link with the grace of the collection stays audible. Readable uses the everyday verb, as the English does in 9:15.

decisions.choice: gracias
decisions.reason: As in 2:14, the grace word here means thanks to God, which Spanish says with its plural "gracias", the same root.

source.text: συνεπέμψαμεν δὲ μετ’ αὐτοῦ τὸν ἀδελφὸν οὗ ὁ ἔπαινος ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ διὰ πασῶν τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν οὐ μόνον δὲ ἀλλὰ καὶ χειροτονηθεὶς ὑπὸ τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν συνέκδημος ἡμῶν σὺν τῇ χάριτι ταύτῃ τῇ διακονουμένῃ ὑφ’ ἡμῶν πρὸς τὴν αὐτοῦ τοῦ κυρίου δόξαν καὶ προθυμίαν ἡμῶν στελλόμενοι τοῦτο μή τις ἡμᾶς μωμήσηται ἐν τῇ ἁδρότητι ταύτῃ τῇ διακονουμένῃ ὑφ’ ἡμῶν, προνοοῦμεν γὰρ καλὰ οὐ μόνον ἐνώπιον κυρίου ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐνώπιον ἀνθρώπων.

records.literal_gloss: We sent with and with him the brother of whom the praise [is] in the gospel through all the churches, \v 19 not only and but also having been appointed by the churches fellow traveler of us with the grace this the [one] being administered by us for the of himself the Lord glory and readiness of us, \v 20 avoiding this, lest anyone us should blame in the generous gift this the [one] being administered by us; \v 21 we take thought for for good things not only before [the] Lord but also before men.

en.L: And we have sent with him the brother whose praise in the gospel [is] through all the churches, \v 19 and not only [that], but also [he] has been appointed by the churches [as] our traveling companion with this grace that is being administered by us for the glory of the Lord {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} and [for] our readiness, \v 20 taking care of this, that no one should blame us in [regard to] this generous gift that is being administered by us; \v 21 for we take thought for what is good, not only before [the] Lord but also before {{gender:people|men}}.
en.B: Traveling with Titus is the brother whose work for the gospel has won him praise in all the churches; we are sending him too. \v 19 Not only that: the churches voted to appoint him as our companion on the journey, as we take charge of this gift of grace. We do it to bring glory to the Lord {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, and because we are eager to help. \v 20 We are guarding against any charge that could be brought against us over this large sum we are handling. \v 21 Our concern is for what is honorable, both before the Lord and before people.
en.R: We are sending another brother along with Titus. All the churches praise him for the way he spreads the good news. \v 19 Also, the churches chose him to travel with us while we take this gift to Jerusalem. We are doing this work to bring glory to the Lord, and to show that we really want to help. \v 20 We are being careful, because this is a lot of money, and we do not want anyone to blame us for the way we handle it. \v 21 We want to do what is right, and not only in the Lord's eyes. We want people to see that it is right too.

fr.L: Et nous avons envoyé avec lui le frère dont la louange dans l’Évangile [se répand] dans toutes les églises, \v 19 et non seulement [cela], mais il a aussi été désigné par les églises [comme] notre compagnon de voyage pour cette grâce qui est administrée par nous pour la gloire du Seigneur {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} et [pour] notre empressement, \v 20 prenant garde à ceci, que personne ne nous blâme au sujet de ce don abondant administré par nous ; \v 21 car nous nous soucions de ce qui est bien, non seulement devant le Seigneur, mais aussi devant les {{gender:humains|hommes}}.
fr.B: Avec Tite, nous envoyons aussi le frère dont le travail pour l’Évangile lui a valu les éloges de toutes les églises. \v 19 Et ce n’est pas tout : les églises l’ont désigné par un vote pour être notre compagnon de voyage, pendant que nous nous occupons de ce don de grâce. Nous le faisons pour la gloire du Seigneur {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, et parce que nous désirons ardemment aider. \v 20 Nous voulons éviter toute accusation qu’on pourrait porter contre nous au sujet de cette somme importante que nous gérons. \v 21 Nous nous soucions de ce qui est honorable, devant le Seigneur comme devant les gens.
fr.R: Nous envoyons un autre frère avec Tite. Toutes les églises le félicitent pour la façon dont il annonce la bonne nouvelle. \v 19 De plus, les églises l’ont choisi pour voyager avec nous pendant que nous apportons ce don à Jérusalem. Nous faisons ce travail pour la gloire du Seigneur, et pour montrer que nous voulons vraiment aider. \v 20 Nous faisons attention, parce que c’est beaucoup d’argent, et nous ne voulons pas qu’on nous reproche la façon dont nous le gérons. \v 21 Nous voulons faire ce qui est juste, et pas seulement aux yeux du Seigneur. Nous voulons que les gens voient aussi que c’est juste.

es.L: Y enviamos con él al hermano cuyo elogio en el evangelio [se extiende] por todas las iglesias; \v 19 y no solo [eso], sino que también fue designado por las iglesias [como] nuestro compañero de viaje con esta gracia que es administrada por nosotros para la gloria del Señor mismo y [para mostrar] nuestra buena disposición, \v 20 evitando esto: que alguien nos culpe en cuanto a esta generosa ofrenda que es administrada por nosotros; \v 21 porque procuramos lo que es bueno, no solo delante del Señor, sino también delante de {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}.
es.B: Con Tito enviamos también al hermano cuyo trabajo por el evangelio le ha ganado el elogio de todas las iglesias. \v 19 Y no solo eso: las iglesias lo eligieron como nuestro compañero de viaje mientras nos encargamos de este don de la gracia. Lo hacemos para dar gloria al Señor mismo, y porque deseamos ayudar. \v 20 Queremos evitar que se nos acuse de algo en relación con esta gran suma que estamos administrando. \v 21 Nos preocupa hacer lo que es honroso, tanto delante del Señor como delante de la gente.
es.R: Junto con Tito enviamos a otro hermano. Todas las iglesias lo elogian por la manera en que anuncia la buena noticia. \v 19 Además, las iglesias lo eligieron para viajar con nosotros mientras llevamos esta ofrenda a Jerusalén. Hacemos este trabajo para dar gloria al Señor y para mostrar que de verdad queremos ayudar. \v 20 Tenemos cuidado, porque esto es mucho dinero, y no queremos que nadie nos culpe por la manera en que lo manejamos. \v 21 Queremos hacer lo correcto, y no solo a los ojos del Señor. Queremos que la gente también vea que es correcto.

decisions.choice: a well-known believer whom Paul does not name
decisions.reason: The Corinthians would know who he was, and Paul's commendation was enough. Many guesses have been made since early times, but the text gives no way to decide. He is a particular man, chosen by the churches.

decisions.choice: praised for his work in spreading the gospel
decisions.reason: "In the gospel" means in the work of the gospel, as in Philippians 4:3. It does not refer to a written Gospel book, a meaning the word does not have in Paul's letters.

decisions.choice: appointed by the churches, probably by a show of hands
decisions.reason: χειροτονηθεὶς first meant to vote by raising the hand, and came to mean to appoint. The churches, probably those of Macedonia, chose him as their representative to travel with the collection, so that it would not rest on Paul's word alone (verse 20; 1 Corinthians 16:3-4).

decisions.choice: this act of grace: the collection
decisions.reason: As in verses 6-7, χάριτι is the collection, a gift that is itself grace at work. Verse 20 calls it a ἁδρότητι, a large or generous gift.

decisions.choice: the purpose of the whole undertaking: the Lord's glory and Paul's eagerness to help
alternatives: the purpose of the brother's appointment
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely goes with the administering of the gift: Paul handles it so that the Lord is honored and his own eagerness is shown. "The Lord" here is probably Christ.

decisions.choice: Paul's sentence runs on loosely: "we are taking care"
alternatives: the participle depends on "we have sent" in verse 18
decisions.reason: The participle στελλόμενοι has no clear main verb to hang on; the long sentence runs on from verse 18. The sense is plain: Paul arranged for an appointed companion so that no one could accuse him of mishandling the money.

decisions.choice: an echo of Proverbs 3:4
decisions.reason: The Greek of Proverbs 3:4 urges taking thought for what is good "before the Lord and men", in almost the same words; Paul uses them again in Romans 12:17. There the Lord stands for the divine name; Paul applies the words to his own conduct.

decisions.choice: people in general, women and men
decisions.reason: ἀνθρώπων is the general word for human beings, set against the Lord.

decisions.choice: grace (L); gift of grace (B); gift (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word to show the wordplay; Balanced says "gift of grace" as in verses 6-7, and Readable "gift" (m4).

decisions.choice: being administered (L); take charge of, handling (B); take, handle (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the "ministry" of verse 4. Here it means managing the fund, so each level uses a word for handling money.

decisions.choice: Lord {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} (L, B); {{gender:people|men}} (L)
decisions.reason: The pronoun for the Lord follows the deity_pronoun setting. Literal's "men" means people in general (m8); Balanced and Readable say "people", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: take this gift to Jerusalem; this is a lot of money
alternatives: this grace being administered by us
decisions.reason: Readable says where the gift was going (verse 4) and why care was needed.

decisions.choice: voted to appoint
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the original sense of the verb (m3).

decisions.choice: l’Évangile (L, B); la bonne nouvelle (R) (for chapters 8-11)
alternatives: la bonne nouvelle at every level
decisions.reason: The style guide's term, as in Colossians: Readable says "bonne nouvelle" because "Évangile" is church language.

decisions.choice: nous envoyons (B, R); nous avons envoyé (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek uses the letter writer's past (the brothers set out with the letter). Literal keeps the past tense; Balanced and Readable say it as the readers will hear it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: el Señor mismo, with no span
decisions.reason: As in 5:20, "mismo" after a noun is an adjective in Spanish and takes no deity_pronoun span, where the English "himself" has one.

decisions.choice: {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}
decisions.reason: As in the English Literal, the traditional "los hombres" is offered as the alternative for the word that means people in general.

source.text: συνεπέμψαμεν δὲ αὐτοῖς τὸν ἀδελφὸν ἡμῶν ὃν ἐδοκιμάσαμεν ἐν πολλοῖς πολλάκις σπουδαῖον ὄντα, νυνὶ δὲ πολὺ σπουδαιότερον πεποιθήσει πολλῇ τῇ εἰς ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: We sent with and them the brother of us whom we tested in many things many times earnest being, now but much more earnest by confidence much the [one] toward you.

en.L: And we have sent with them our brother, whom we have tested many times in many things [and found] to be eager, but now much more eager because of [his] great confidence in you.
en.B: With them we are also sending our brother. Time after time and in many situations we have put him to the test and found him eager, and he is more eager than ever now, because he has great confidence in you.
en.R: We are also sending another brother with them. We have tested him many times in many ways, and he has always been eager to help. Now he is even more eager, because he trusts you so much.

fr.L: Et nous avons envoyé avec eux notre frère, que nous avons souvent mis à l’épreuve en bien des choses [et trouvé] empressé, mais maintenant beaucoup plus empressé à cause de [sa] grande confiance en vous.
fr.B: Avec eux, nous envoyons aussi notre frère. À maintes reprises et en bien des situations, nous l’avons mis à l’épreuve et nous l’avons trouvé plein d’empressement ; il l’est maintenant plus que jamais, parce qu’il a une grande confiance en vous.
fr.R: Nous envoyons aussi un autre frère avec eux. Nous l’avons mis à l’épreuve souvent et de bien des manières, et il a toujours été prêt à aider. Maintenant, il l’est encore plus, parce qu’il vous fait très confiance.

es.L: Y enviamos con ellos a nuestro hermano, a quien hemos puesto a prueba muchas veces en muchas cosas [y hallado] diligente, pero ahora mucho más diligente por la gran confianza [que tiene] en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Con ellos enviamos también a nuestro hermano. Muchas veces y en muchas situaciones lo hemos puesto a prueba y lo hemos encontrado diligente, y ahora lo está más que nunca, porque tiene una gran confianza en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: También enviamos con ellos a otro hermano. Lo hemos puesto a prueba muchas veces y de muchas maneras, y siempre ha estado dispuesto a ayudar. Ahora tiene todavía más ganas, porque confía mucho en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

decisions.choice: a second believer whom Paul does not name, a particular man
decisions.reason: "Our brother" probably means one of Paul's own fellow workers, as against the brother of verse 18, who was chosen by the churches. Paul does not name him.

decisions.choice: the brother's confidence in the Corinthians
decisions.reason: The phrase most naturally describes the brother: he is more eager because he trusts the Corinthians. It may also reflect what Paul and Titus had told him (7:14-16).

decisions.choice: tested and proven
decisions.reason: ἐδοκιμάσαμεν is the verb of verse 8, to test so as to prove genuine. The brother has passed the test many times.

decisions.choice: [and found] to be eager
decisions.reason: English needs a verb to join the test and its result.

source.text: εἴτε ὑπὲρ Τίτου, κοινωνὸς ἐμὸς καὶ εἰς ὑμᾶς συνεργός· εἴτε ἀδελφοὶ ἡμῶν, ἀπόστολοι ἐκκλησιῶν, δόξα Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Whether about Titus, partner mine and for you fellow worker; whether brothers of us, apostles of churches, glory of Christ.

en.L: Whether [it is] about Titus, [he is] my partner and fellow worker for you; or [about] our brothers, [they are] messengers of churches, [the] glory of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: If anyone asks about Titus: he is a partner of mine, working with me for you. If they ask about our brothers: they are envoys of the churches, and they bring glory to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: Titus is my partner. He works with me to help you. And the other brothers have been sent by the churches. They bring glory to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

fr.L: Pour ce qui est de Tite, [il est] mon associé et mon collaborateur auprès de vous ; pour ce qui est de nos frères, [ils sont] des envoyés des églises, [la] gloire du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Si l’on vous interroge sur Tite : il est mon associé, il travaille avec moi pour vous. Si l’on vous interroge sur nos frères : ce sont les délégués des églises, et ils contribuent à la gloire du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.R: Tite est mon associé. Il travaille avec moi pour vous aider. Et les autres frères ont été envoyés par les églises. Ils servent à la gloire du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.

es.L: En cuanto a Tito, [es] mi compañero y colaborador para con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; en cuanto a nuestros hermanos, [son] enviados de [las] iglesias, gloria {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}.
es.B: Si alguien pregunta por Tito, es mi compañero, que trabaja conmigo por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Si preguntan por nuestros hermanos, son delegados de las iglesias, y dan gloria {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}.
es.R: Tito es mi compañero. Trabaja conmigo para {{plural_you:ayudarlos|ayudaros}}. Y a los otros hermanos los han enviado las iglesias. Ellos dan gloria {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}.

decisions.choice: messengers sent by the churches, not apostles like Paul
alternatives: apostles of Christ, like Paul and the Twelve
decisions.reason: ἀπόστολοι means someone sent with a commission. Paul uses it for himself and others sent by Christ, but here these men are sent "by churches", as their envoys for the collection, just as Epaphroditus was the Philippians' messenger (Philippians 2:25).

decisions.choice: partner: one who shares in Paul's work
decisions.reason: κοινωνὸς belongs to the partnership words of verse 4 and of Philippians (1:5, 7; Philemon 17). Titus shares fully in Paul's work, and he works with Paul for the Corinthians' good.

decisions.choice: they bring glory to Christ
alternatives: they show Christ's glory in their lives
decisions.reason: "The glory of Christ" says what these men are: people whose lives and work honor Christ. The phrase may also mean that Christ's glory is seen in them (3:18); either way the Corinthians should welcome them.

decisions.choice: a compressed commendation: "whether ... or"
decisions.reason: The sentence has no verbs. Paul lists the credentials of the men he is sending, as if answering anyone who asks who they are.

decisions.choice: messengers of churches (L); envoys of the churches (B); sent by the churches (R)
decisions.reason: "Apostles" would make readers think of Paul and the Twelve (m1). Philippians 2:25 has "messenger" (Literal) and "envoy" (Balanced) for the same word, and this verse follows it.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: they bring glory to
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how these men are Christ's glory (m3).

decisions.choice: des envoyés (L); les délégués (B); envoyés par (R)
decisions.reason: As in English, "apôtres" would make readers think of Paul and the Twelve (m1). "Délégués" says that the churches chose and sent them; "messagers" would suggest that they only carry a message.

decisions.choice: enviados (L); delegados (B); los han enviado (R)
decisions.reason: The word is the one usually rendered "apostles", but here it means messengers sent by the churches (meaning decision); "apóstoles" would make them apostles like Paul.

source.text: τὴν οὖν ἔνδειξιν τῆς ἀγάπης ὑμῶν καὶ ἡμῶν καυχήσεως ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν εἰς αὐτοὺς ἐνδεικνύμενοι εἰς πρόσωπον τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν.

records.literal_gloss: The therefore proof of the love of you and of our boasting about you to them showing, in face of the churches.

en.L: Therefore, [be] showing to them the proof of your love and of our boasting about you, before the face of the churches.
en.B: So, with the churches looking on, give these men proof of your love, and let them see why we have been proud of you.
en.R: So show these men that your love is real. Show them that we were right to be proud of you. Then all the churches will see it.

fr.L: Montrez-leur donc la preuve de votre amour et de notre sujet de fierté à votre égard, à la face des églises.
fr.B: Alors, sous les yeux des églises, donnez à ces hommes la preuve de votre amour, et montrez-leur pourquoi nous avons été fiers de vous.
fr.R: Alors montrez à ces hommes que votre amour est vrai. Montrez-leur que nous avions raison d’être fiers de vous. Ainsi, toutes les églises le verront.

es.L: Por tanto, {{plural_you:muestren|mostrad}} ante ellos, delante de las iglesias, la prueba de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} amor y de nuestro gloriarnos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Así que, con las iglesias como testigos, {{plural_you:den|dad}} a estos hombres la prueba de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} amor, y {{plural_you:háganles|hacedles}} ver por qué nos sentimos orgullosos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:muestren|mostrad}} a estos hombres que {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} amor es auténtico. {{plural_you:Muéstrenles|Mostradles}} que teníamos razón al estar orgullosos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Entonces todas las iglesias lo verán.

decisions.choice: a command: show them
alternatives: a description of what they are doing
decisions.reason: The participle ἐνδεικνύμενοι stands where a command would be, as participles sometimes do in Paul's appeals (Romans 12:9-13). The sense is a request.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: the participle "showing"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts have an imperative verb here, which says outright what the participle implies. The meaning is the same. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: before the churches: the messengers represent them
decisions.reason: The brothers come as envoys of the churches (verse 23). How the Corinthians receive them will be reported to those churches.

decisions.choice: boasting: Paul's proud confidence in the Corinthians
decisions.reason: καυχήσεως is the boasting Paul did to Titus about them (7:14) and to the Macedonians (9:2-3). It is good pride; Paul asks them to show it was justified.

decisions.choice: boasting (L); proud (B, R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide choice: Literal keeps "boasting"; Balanced and Readable say "proud", since this is good pride and Paul's argument does not turn on the word itself.

decisions.choice: with the churches looking on
alternatives: before the face of the churches
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the setting first so that the two things they are to show stand together.
